governing_note: B2.6-P2 Corrective XVIII (H-XVIII-R11/R12): the sovereign supported-event-family law. The ONLY authority for 'this payload denotes a financial family' is derive_event_family() over verified provider bytes (backend/app/webhooks/commerce_derivation.py), bound into b26_p2_provider_auth_consequence.b26_p2_event_family inside the sovereign atomic under the per-provider allowlist below. Relay route selection is advisory/defense-in-depth only and can never confer family. Signal-less shapes are accepted ONLY under the explicit family-implicit disposition recorded per provider: the shape itself is the provider's canonical representation of the supported family, and every other family of that provider arrives in a distinct refused-or-typed shape. This artifact is subordinate to the semantic regime: a family-law change requires a new semantic regime (registry-append), never an in-place edit.

stripe.signal_rule: a present type/event_type must alias the canonical family or the payload is REFUSED (e.g. charge.refunded, payment_intent.payment_failed); status=succeeded attests the canonical family; any other present status is REFUSED
family_implicit_shapes: flat payment_intent object {id, amount, currency, created}
stripe.family_implicit_rationale: a bare payment_intent object carries no state field; every non-succeeded Stripe family (refunds, failures, disputes, checkout sessions) arrives in a distinct typed object or envelope that this contract refuses or that carries a refusing type signal. The flat object is therefore the provider's canonical representation of the succeeded family, and the disposition is recorded here -- not inferred from the relay URL.

shopify.signal_rule: the contracted order JSON carries no provider family signal; family authority rests on the order shape itself (defense in depth: the relay additionally checks the X-Shopify-Topic header, but the root does not trust headers)
shopify.family_implicit_rationale: Shopify order webhooks for distinct lifecycle events share the order shape; P2 supports exactly one financial family (orders.create) and exactly one financial fact per order (identity law). A refund/dispute lifecycle event for the same order carries a distinct topic and no new financial fact within the supported scope; it is excluded at ingestion scope, never coerced into a second canonical lineage (commerce-identity conservation).

paypal.signal_rule: a present event_type must alias the canonical family or the payload is REFUSED (e.g. PAYMENT.SALE.DENIED); signal-less flat sale JSON is family-implicit
family_implicit_shapes: flat sale JSON {id, amount{total, currency}, create_time}
paypal.family_implicit_rationale: the contracted flat sale shape is PayPal's completed-sale representation; resource-enveloped webhooks (all other sale lifecycle events) are refused outright, so no other family can arrive in this shape.

woocommerce.signal_rule: a present status must be completed (or alias the canonical family) or the payload is REFUSED (e.g. refunded); signal-less order JSON is family-implicit under the governed completion/date_created timestamp law
family_implicit_shapes: order JSON {id, total, currency, date_completed and/or date_created}
woocommerce.family_implicit_rationale: completion status, when the provider states it, must read completed; when unstated, the order-total shape under the governed timestamp law denotes the completed-order financial fact. Distinct lifecycle states that the provider states explicitly are refused, never coerced.

conservation: CURRENT TRUST = AUTHENTICATED BYTES + SUPPORTED FAMILY + CURRENT REGIME. Break any term and no financial authority exists.
